name: Fluence
tagline: Speak off the cuff, get honest coaching on how you actually spoke.
description:
Fluence is a spontaneous-speech coach that lives in a GIF.

Pick a drill — freestyle, or one of nine types from the catalog — and record a take. GifOS records through its own visible recorder, so the app does not hold the live microphone. You get a transcript of what you said, then a score on the things that actually matter: how fast you spoke, how clearly, how often you paused, filled, hedged, or restarted, how varied your words were, and how sure the transcript is.

Only then does a language model weigh in, with rules that match the drill — a listing task is graded on how many items you named, a story on whether it has a beginning and an end. You get coaching that quotes what you said, a suggested next drill aimed at your top weakness, and a weekly review that tracks whether any of it is working. Picture-description drills draw their own scene.

Every take, review and benchmark stays private, saved with the app on your Home Screen.
